statement.p:
Shown below is a matrix and its reduced row echelon form. Indicate the pivot positions.
\left[ \begin{array}{rrrr} 2 \amp 4 \amp 6 \amp -1 \\ -3 \amp 1 \amp 5 \amp 0 \\ 1 \amp 3 \amp 5 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[ \begin{array}{rrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right] .

How many pivot positions can there be in one row? In a 3\times5 matrix, what is the largest possible number of pivot positions? Give an example of a 3\times5 matrix that has the largest possible number of pivot positions.

solution.p:
A row contains at most one pivot position. Therefore, a 3\times 5 matrix, which has three rows, contains at most three pivot positions. Here is an example:
\left[\begin{array}{rrrrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \amp 1 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \amp 2 \amp 3 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.}

statement.p: How many pivots can there be in one column? In a 5\times3 matrix, what is the largest possible number of pivot positions? Give an example of a 5\times3 matrix that has the largest possible number of pivot positions.

solution.p:
A column contains at most one pivot position. Therefore, a 5\times 3 matrix, which has three columns, contains at most three pivot positions. Here is an example
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.}

statement.p: Give an example of a matrix with a pivot position in every row and every column. What is special about such a matrix?

answer.p: Such a matrix must necessarily have the same number of rows and columns, which means it is what we call a square matrix.
